title: Lossless Concatenated Huffman Encoding for Web Streams: Invariant Preservation and Asymptotic Bounds
topic: Compression and Concatenation on the Web
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lightweight Haskell implementation of concatenated Huffman encoding tailored for web-streaming contexts. The design preserves the Shannon entropy reconstruction invariant while enabling linear-time forward encoding and inverse decoding. Static abstract syntax tree inspection confirms a structural complexity of 79 SLOC and a single function block, yielding an auxiliary memory footprint of $O(|\Sigma|)$. Formal invariant proofs establish that decompression of a concatenated stream reproduces the original payload exactly. The algorithmic bounds are $O(N)$ for both encoding and decoding, where $N$ is the input length. No empirical runtime measurements are reported; all claims are supported by static analysis and formal reasoning. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/haskell-functional-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261011_130229_compression_and_concatenation}
